title: [CQ-V01] Protected required check definitions

User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

implementationPlan.note:
I loaded adversarial-self-review and attacked the V01 diff (dc13b0e+d8f2d6e) on the 4 files at HEAD. No defects, so no bytes changed.

- Change, delete or add a protected file:
  - protectedDrift compares the union of approved and candidate paths. A changed oid, a missing path or an added path under a root each produce a token.
  - Duplicate, non-string or non-array entries return null, which yields protected-checks-unmeasured.
  - Paths that are not normalized get filtered out, which makes the approved path look missing, so they fail closed too.
  - Roots are always normalized: normalizeAffectedFile plus the validator's `entry === normalized` reject a trailing '/', '', '..' and absolute paths. That keeps the `${root}/` boundary exact.
- Another command, another tree, or an agent-reported run: passedOn requires the same candidateId, the same treeSha, a trimmed exact command match, exit 0 and source runner-observed. owed() checks each approved command separately.
- Missing, garbled or stale snapshot:
  - The policy reports protected-checks-unapproved, and a validator throw reports the same.
  - The projection returns false; protected tokens are checked before checkOwed.
  - getContext omits the overlay. readRequiredCheckSnapshot wraps everything in try/catch, so it never throws.
- Live versus approved definitions: the policy reads the live requiredChecks only after the snapshot's digest check passes. definitionDigest covers id, command, configs, scripts and assertionRoots, and both reads are synchronous on one task object, so the result equals the approved definitions. getContext serves only the decoded snapshot.
- Error handling: the lookup try/catch returns unmeasured plus every owed command, and test (e) proves it. There are no writes, no awaits and no shared mutation, so no race. Maps are used, not plain objects, so a '__proto__' path is safe. Both entry lists are capped at 2000.

Theoretical, out of V01 scope:
(1) record_check_run's source is caller-declared (audience W/Q). That predates V01, and CQ-V03 owns authenticating it. record_candidate is wrapper-only.
(2) The legacy policy skips protected checks, by design.
(3) An IDE UPDATE_TASK edit to executionContract (it is not on the denylist) makes the snapshot stale. The policy then fails closed. C01's packet manifest lists the conditional overlay only when it is served, so the omission is not flagged; requiredChecks is still served. Candidate for V12/C11.
